Sponsor Us

Help keep hands-on engineering accessible to our students.

As a high-cost student engineering program with no school funding, we depend heavily on sponsors, grants, and in-kind support to keep these opportunities accessible.

A robot takes more than just engineering. It starts with hundreds of individual components and students willing to turn them into one. Team 867 currently operates with limited funding, while the cost of competing continues to rise. Our immediate priority is ensuring that we are able to participate in both of our major engineering seasons.

Talk with our teamDownload sponsorship packet (PDF)

Where your support goes

FIRST Robotics registration~ $7,000

Our largest single expense; registration is required before our students can even compete.

Minimum robot build~ $6,000

Even a basic competitive FRC robot requires thousands of dollars in components.

JPL / Wonderworks season~ $2,000

Before FRC even begins, three smaller student teams prototype and manufacture completely separate engineering devices for the JPL challenge. Funding will support prototyping materials, motors & electronics, wood/metal, and transportation.

Approximate program costs from our 2026–2027 packet. These are not sponsorship tier prices.

Robot components

  • Motors
  • Aluminum & steel
  • Limelight vision camera
  • Robot radio
  • Motor controllers, sensors & encoders
  • Bearings, belts, chain & gears

Building our workshop

Today, much of Team 867’s manufacturing is performed using basic tools: Drills, Saws, Bandsaw, Drill Press, Hand Tools.

Those tools teach valuable skills, but they also limit the complexity and precision of what students can manufacture.

One of our long-term goals is to build a fund that goes toward purchasing practical equipment such as a CNC machine, allowing students to manufacture more advanced robot components themselves while learning industry-relevant machining skills.

Therefore, your sponsorship helps us compete today and build our engineering capabilities for tomorrow.
